title: Changing a public API field from number to string
hidden_flaw: Changing `id` from number to string in v1 responses breaks existing typed clients (mobile apps with strict decoders, generated SDKs) that cannot be force-upgraded; old app versions stay in the wild for months. Requires additive change (new field `id_str` / new API version), deprecation window and telemetry on client versions.
notes: Fundamental flaw: in-place type change of a field consumed by clients that cannot be upgraded in lockstep.

input.objective: Fix ID precision loss: order IDs are now Snowflake 64-bit integers and JavaScript clients corrupt them above 2^53.
constraints: Public REST API v1 is used by our iOS/Android apps and ~40 partner integrations.
Mobile app versions older than 6 months are still ~18% of traffic; forced upgrade is not allowed by product.
Partners were promised 6 months notice for breaking changes.
input.context: GET /v1/orders/{id} and list endpoints return `"id": 1234567890123456789` as a JSON number. The web frontend already shows wrong IDs for new orders. iOS uses Codable with `let id: Int64`; Android uses Moshi with `val id: Long`; partner SDKs are generated from our OpenAPI spec (type: integer, format: int64).
input.proposed_solution: Change the `id` field in all v1 responses to a JSON string (e.g. "1234567890123456789") and update the OpenAPI spec to `type: string`. Strings are the industry standard for 64-bit IDs (Twitter did the same), and since the numeric value does not change, clients just need to read it as a string. Ship it in the next weekly release and post a changelog entry.
